react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge unambiguously on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway in this treatment-vs-control comparison. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned KEGG:hsa00380 (map00380) as the top hit with FDR = 1.08e-15 and fold-enrichment = 858, implicating six input metabolites — quinolinic acid, melatonin, tryptamine, L-tryptophan, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and serotonin. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA reproduced the same KEGG:hsa00380 at rank 1 with raw p = 1.79e-07, hitting the same five tryptophan-derived compounds. Mummichog's empirical m/z network independently identified tryptophan metabolism as its top-ranked pathway (p = 8.4e-05, overlap 13/14 metabolites), capturing the same six core metabolites plus L-tryptophan stereoisomer noise. The three-tool consensus — across ORA, m/z network, and community-standard KEGG PSEA — is unbroken and ranks no other pathway above tryptophan metabolism in any paradigm. Six of the eight input compounds belong to this pathway: L-tryptophan feeds the serotonin/melatonin branch (via tryptamine) and the kynurenine/quinolinic acid branch (via 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid), with serotonin acting as the branching point to melatonin. The two outliers, L-proline and molybdenum (KEGG:C00150), did not register in any significant pathway hit. The biological picture is a coordinated perturbation of tryptophan catabolism affecting both neuroactive (serotonin–melatonin) and NAD+-biosynthetic (kynurenine–quinolinic acid) arms, consistent with inflammation, neuroimmune activation, or microbiome-mediated tryptophan depletion in the treatment condition.
